examples.en: Our baby has started taking first steps.
The baby fell while practicing walking.

examples.ko: 걸음마가 빠른 아이도 있고 느린 아이도 있어요.
examples.en: Some children walk early and some walk late.

examples.ko: 할머니가 걸음마 하는 아기 손을 잡아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma held the hand of the baby learning to walk.

examples.ko: 걸음마 신발은 가볍고 미끄럽지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: Shoes for toddlers should be light and non-slip.

examples.ko: 사진 속 아기는 아직 걸음마도 못 하는 때였어요.
examples.en: In the photo, the baby was at an age before even taking first steps.

explain: 아기가 처음 걷기 시작하는 것을 '걸음마를 시작하다', 걷는 데 익숙해진 것을 '걸음마를 떼다'라고 해요. '걸음마'는 걷는 동작 자체를 가리켜서 '걸음'과 달라요. 어른의 일에 쓰면 비유가 되는데 아래 표현을 보세요.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 해외 시장에서는 아직 걸음마 단계예요.
phrases.en: in its infancy; just getting started
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 이제 막 시작해서 아직 많이 부족한 상태를 아기의 걸음마에 빗대요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares a field that has only just started, and is still immature, to a baby's first steps.

explain_en: '걸음마를 시작하다' means a baby begins to walk, and '걸음마를 떼다' means the baby has got the hang of it. '걸음마' is the early walking itself, not just a step. For adults it becomes a metaphor; see below.

examples.en: I hit the nail hard with a hammer.

examples.ko: 화가 난 듯 책상을 주먹으로 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: As if angry, he pounded the desk with his fist.
I was startled by the sound of lightning striking down.

examples.ko: 선생님이 화가 나서 칠판을 손으로 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: The teacher got angry and slammed the blackboard with their hand.
Be careful when you bring the axe down on firewood.

examples.ko: 선수가 공을 위에서 아래로 세게 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: The player smashed the ball hard from above.

explain: 그냥 '치다'와 달리 위에서 아래로 힘껏 때리는 방향이 분명해요. 망치나 주먹뿐 아니라 번개가 떨어질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 화가 나서 주먹으로 문을 내려쳤어요.
phrases.en: He was angry and struck the door with his fist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주먹으로'와 함께 도구나 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '주먹으로', it states the tool or method used.

phrases.en: The teacher slammed the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로 이미 일어난 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form for something that already happened.

phrases.en: I struck the tree hard with an axe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세게'를 붙이면 힘이 센 정도가 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '세게' makes the strength of the blow clearer.

explain_en: Unlike plain '치다', the downward direction of the blow is clear. It is used for hammers and fists, and also for lightning striking down.

examples.en: He kept fiddling with his handkerchief, probably because he was nervous.
Please don't fiddle with your pen during class.

examples.ko: 휴대폰만 만지작거리고 있지 말고 이야기를 해요.
examples.en: Don't just fiddle with your phone; let's talk.
My friend twirled her hair as she thought it over.

examples.ko: 아이가 주머니 속 동전을 자꾸 만지작거려요.
examples.en: The child keeps fingering the coins in his pocket.

examples.ko: 사지도 않을 물건을 만지작거리면 직원이 불편해해요.
examples.en: Staff get uncomfortable if you keep fiddling with things you won't buy.

explain: '만지다'와 달리 손으로 계속 조금씩 건드리는 모습이고, 긴장·고민·심심함 때문에 무심코 할 때가 많아요. '만지작대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: The child keeps fiddling with the toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만지작거리다'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 짧게 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만지작거리다, in a slightly shorter form.

phrases.en: He's just fiddling with his phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할 일이 없거나 불안할 때 손에 든 물건을 만지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes touching something in your hand when bored or anxious.

phrases.en: Please don't keep fiddling with the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 손대는 행동을 말릴 때 쓰는 부탁이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request to stop someone from constantly fidgeting with something.

explain_en: Unlike '만지다' (to touch), it describes touching something repeatedly in small movements, often unconsciously from nervousness, worry or boredom. '만지작대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I feel proud hearing the compliment.

examples.ko: 아이가 상을 받고 으쓱한 얼굴로 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The child came back with a proud face after winning a prize.
Being praised in front of friends made my shoulders lift proudly.
Wearing new shoes makes me feel proud for no reason.
He shrugged his shoulders and avoided answering.
My younger sibling got puffed up and started bragging.

explain: 칭찬이나 좋은 일 때문에 우쭐해지고 기분이 좋아질 때 많이 써요. 어깨를 한번 올리는 동작에도 쓸 수 있지만 일상에서는 '어깨가 으쓱하다'처럼 기분을 말하는 쓰임이 흔해요. 부사 '으쓱'과 짝이에요.

phrases.en: I felt proud after being praised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분이 점점 우쭐해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you gradually feel proud.

phrases.en: I felt proud because I won a prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun.

phrases.en: He shrugged as if he didn't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어깨를 올리는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of raising the shoulders.

explain_en: It is often used when praise or good news makes you feel puffed up and happy. It can also describe lifting the shoulders, but in daily life the feeling sense, like '어깨가 으쓱하다', is common. It pairs with the adverb '으쓱'.

examples.en: I only picked up this information from a friend, so I'm not sure.
I picked up guitar by listening in from the sidelines.
I overheard that rumor while passing by.

examples.ko: 그냥 주워들어서 아는 건데 아마 맞을 거예요.
examples.en: I only know it from hearing it around, but it's probably right.

examples.ko: 어디서 주워들었는지 아이가 어려운 말을 해요.
examples.en: I don't know where he picked it up, but the child uses difficult words.
He has a habit of eavesdropping on other people's talk.

explain: 직접 배우거나 확인한 게 아니라 여기저기서 우연히 들어서 알게 된 것에 써요. '귀동냥'과 비슷하고, 정확하지 않다는 느낌이 조금 있어요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라서 '주워들어요, 주워들은'이 돼요.

phrases.en: It's something I overheard, so I don't know if it's true.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확하지 않은 소문이나 정보를 말할 때 '-ㄴ' 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used for uncertain rumors or information.

phrases.en: I picked up that story from somewhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출처가 확실하지 않을 때 '어디선가'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 어디선가 when the source is unclear.

phrases.en: I learned a little by listening in nearby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주워듣다'와 비슷한 말인데 남이 하는 말을 곁에서 듣고 배우는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 주워듣다 but with more of a sense of learning by listening to others nearby.

explain_en: Use it for things you learned by overhearing here and there rather than studying or checking them. It is close to '귀동냥' and carries a slight sense that the knowledge may not be accurate. It is a 'ㄷ'-irregular verb: '주워들어요', '주워들은'.

examples.en: Someone behind me keeps giggling.
My friends giggled during class and got scolded.

examples.ko: 아이들이 이불 속에서 키득거리는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the kids giggling under the blanket.
I giggled to myself while reading a text.

examples.ko: 그 얘기만 들으면 나도 모르게 키득거리게 돼요.
examples.en: Whenever I hear that story, I giggle without meaning to.
Stop giggling and listen seriously.

explain: 웃음을 참으며 낮고 작게 웃는 모습이에요. '깔깔거리다'는 소리 내어 크게 웃는 느낌이라 다르고, '킥킥거리다'와는 비슷해요. 누군가 몰래 웃거나 놀리는 느낌으로 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: My friend is giggling under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키득거리다'와 비슷하고 더 짧고 빠른 웃음이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 키득거리다 but a shorter, quicker laugh.

phrases.en: The kids laughed with giggles.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 웃는 모습을 이어서 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -며 to connect and describe the way of laughing.

phrases.en: We need to be quiet, so please don't giggle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음소리를 내지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to make giggling sounds.

explain_en: It describes laughing low and softly while trying to hold the laughter in. '깔깔거리다' is a loud, open laugh, so it differs, while '킥킥거리다' is similar. It can also carry a sense of laughing secretly or teasingly.

en: to throb; to palpitate; to beat

examples.ko: 발표 전에 가슴이 너무 두근대서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My heart was pounding so much before the presentation that I couldn't sleep.
My heart pounds when I meet the person I like.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리면서 두근대는 마음을 진정시켰어요.
examples.en: While waiting for the exam results, I calmed my racing heart.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타기 전부터 가슴이 두근대기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My heart started pounding even before I got on the ride.
My heart was pounding when I opened the letter.
I don't know why my heart is pounding like this.

explain: '두근거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 주로 '가슴이/심장이 두근대요'처럼 말하고, 설렘, 긴장, 놀람에 모두 써요. '두근두근'이라는 부사와 같이 '가슴이 두근두근해요'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 가슴이 두근거렸어요.
phrases.en: My heart pounded while I waited for my test results.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두근대다'와 뜻이 같고, 말과 글에서 조금 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 두근대다 and a bit more common in speech and writing.

phrases.example: 내일 여행을 간다고 생각하니 가슴이 두근두근해요.
phrases.en: My heart is thumping thinking about tomorrow's trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두근두근'을 붙이면 심장이 뛰는 소리와 느낌이 더 생생해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 두근두근 makes the heartbeat sound and feeling more vivid.

phrases.en: With a fluttering heart, I opened the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요. 설레는 분위기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -는 ending modifies the noun; it suits an excited mood.

explain_en: It means the same as '두근거리다' and the two can be swapped. It is usually used as '가슴이/심장이 두근대요' and covers excitement, nervousness and surprise. People also say '가슴이 두근두근해요' with the adverb '두근두근'.

en: inside the bones; marrow; deep down

examples.en: The cold wind cut right into my bones.
It's a day so cold it chills you to the bone.
The doctor said an infection has developed inside the bone.
Those words stayed with me deep down.
He is a Seoulite through and through.
That child is a prankster to the core.

explain: 뼛속은 실제로는 뼈 안쪽이지만 일상에서는 '뼛속까지 춥다'처럼 아주 깊고 강한 느낌을 말해요. '골수팬'의 '골수'는 뼈 안의 골수(骨髓)에서 온 말이라서, 마음 깊이 열성적인 팬을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: to be something to the core
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습만이 아니라 성격과 습관까지 완전히 그렇다는 뜻이에요. 사람의 성격이나 직업, 출신을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is that way not just on the surface but in character and habits. Used for a person's nature, job, or background.
phrases.en_equiv: to the core; through and through

explain_en: 뼛속 literally means the inside of a bone, but in daily speech it conveys something deep and intense, as in 뼛속까지 춥다. The 골수 in 골수팬 (a die-hard fan) comes from bone marrow (骨髓), so it refers to a fan devoted deep down.

examples.en: I mended the pants that had a hole.
The dry cleaner's will alter and mend clothes for you.
I went to have my jeans hemmed.

examples.ko: 낡은 구두를 수선하면 더 오래 신을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you repair old shoes, you can wear them longer.

examples.ko: 이 가방 끈은 수선할 수 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked if the strap on this bag can be repaired.
Mom mended the ripped blanket herself.

explain: 옷, 신발, 가방처럼 천이나 가죽으로 된 물건을 고칠 때 써요. 기계나 전자 제품은 '고치다'나 '수리하다'를 써서 '수선'은 맞지 않아요. 옷을 맡길 때는 '수선을 맡기다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I left my pants for alteration to shorten them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 고쳐 달라고 가게에 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you hand clothes to a shop for fixing.

phrases.en: I had a new zipper put on at the alteration shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 고쳐 주는 가게 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a shop that repairs clothes.

phrases.en: I mend my old coat and keep wearing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고친 다음에 계속 쓴다는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form meaning you mend it and keep using it.

explain_en: It is used for fixing items made of fabric or leather, such as clothes, shoes, and bags. For machines and electronics, use '고치다' or '수리하다' instead; '수선' doesn't fit. When you hand over clothes for fixing, you say '수선을 맡기다'.

examples.ko: 갑자기 문이 열려서 등이 오싹 차가워졌어요.
examples.en: The door suddenly opened, and my back went cold.

examples.ko: 귀신 이야기를 듣다가 오싹 소름이 돋았어요.
examples.en: Listening to a ghost story gave me goosebumps.

examples.ko: 찬 바람이 불자 몸이 오싹 떨렸어요.
examples.en: When the cold wind blew, my body shivered.

examples.ko: 어두운 골목에서 누가 쳐다보는 것 같아 오싹했어요.
examples.en: In the dark alley it felt like someone was watching me, and I got chills.
Watching a horror movie gives you the chills even in summer.
I got a chilly feeling and turned around.

explain: '오싹'은 무서움과 추위 둘 다에 써요. 무서운 느낌이 더 날카로우면 '섬뜩하다', 분위기가 음산하면 '으스스하다'를 써요. 보통 '오싹하다', '등골이 오싹하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 너무 오싹해서 밤에 혼자 못 봐요.
phrases.en: That movie is so creepy that I can't watch it alone at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오싹'에 '-하다'를 붙인 형용사로, 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adjective form with -하다 and the most basic usage.

phrases.example: 어두운 골목에서 소리가 나서 등골이 오싹했어요.
phrases.en: I heard a sound in the dark alley and a chill ran down my spine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 무섭거나 놀랐을 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common expression when suddenly scared or shocked.
phrases.en_equiv: to get chills down one's spine

phrases.en: Being home alone at night made me feel a chill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해지다'를 붙여 기분이 변해 가는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해지다 shows the feeling changing into a chill.

explain_en: '오싹' works for both fear and cold. For a sharper scary feeling use '섬뜩하다', and for a gloomy atmosphere use '으스스하다'. It usually appears as '오싹하다' or '등골이 오싹하다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈을 초롱초롱 빛내며 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: The child listens to the story with bright, sparkling eyes.
Stars twinkle clearly in the countryside night sky.
My puppy looked up at me with bright eyes.

examples.ko: 학생들이 초롱초롱 빛나는 눈으로 발표를 들었어요.
examples.en: The students listened to the presentation with sparkling eyes.

examples.ko: 잠을 푹 잤더니 눈이 초롱초롱 맑아요.
examples.en: After a good sleep, my eyes are bright and clear.

examples.ko: 아기가 초롱초롱 쳐다보는 얼굴을 보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Seeing the baby's face gazing up with bright eyes makes me smile.

explain: 주로 눈이나 별이 맑고 또렷하게 빛나는 모습에 써요. 같은 뿌리의 형용사가 '초롱초롱하다'예요. '반짝반짝'보다 맑고 정신이 또렷한 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: The child looked at me with bright, clear eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 바꿔 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.example: 아이들이 눈을 초롱초롱하게 뜨고 선생님을 봐요.
phrases.en: The children keep their eyes bright and wide open and look at the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하게' 형태로도 같은 뜻으로 자연스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '하게' form is used naturally with the same meaning.

phrases.en: He is a child whose eyes sparkle clearly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 눈을 설명할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing a person's eyes.

explain_en: It is mostly used for eyes or stars shining clear and bright. The adjective with the same root is '초롱초롱하다'. Compared with '반짝반짝', it gives a stronger sense of clearness and alertness.

examples.en: This rubber ball is still firm and bouncy.
Your skin looks firm and plump.
The noodles are springy, so they are satisfying to chew.

examples.ko: 탱탱한 풍선을 만지니까 터질 것 같아요.
examples.en: When I touch the tight balloon, it feels like it will burst.
After a massage, my face became firmer.
This jelly has set firm and bouncy.

explain: '탱탱하다'는 눌러도 도로 튀어 오를 만큼 속이 차고 탄력 있는 느낌이에요. '팽팽하다'는 줄이 당겨진 모습에도 쓰지만 탱탱하다는 피부, 면, 고무공처럼 탄력 있는 것에 써요. 말랑한 것은 '말랑말랑하다', 쫄깃한 것은 '쫄깃하다'라고 달리 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 탱탱한 피부를 오래 유지하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to keep my skin firm and bouncy for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때는 '탱탱한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '탱탱한' when it describes a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This shop is popular for its springy noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국수가 쫄깃하고 탄력 있게 잘 삶아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when noodles are cooked well and are chewy and springy.

phrases.en: It's an old ball, so it isn't bouncy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탄력이 없어졌다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the negative form to say that something has lost its bounce.

explain_en: 탱탱하다 describes something full and springy that bounces back when pressed. 팽팽하다 can also describe a stretched string, but 탱탱하다 is for elastic things like skin, noodles and rubber balls. Soft things are 말랑말랑하다 and chewy things are 쫄깃하다.

examples.en: I was thirsty and drank the water in one gulp.
The child swallowed the pill in one gulp.
I was nervous and swallowed hard.

examples.ko: 쓴 약이었지만 눈을 감고 꿀꺽 넘겼어요.
examples.en: The medicine was bitter, but I closed my eyes and got it down in one gulp.

examples.ko: 그는 꿀꺽 소리가 크게 나도록 주스를 다 마셨어요.
examples.en: He drank all the juice with a loud gulp.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 간식을 몰래 꿀꺽해 버렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling secretly gobbled up my snack.

explain: 꿀꺽은 음식이나 물을 한 번에 크게 삼키는 소리와 모양에 써요. 여러 번 마시면 '꿀꺽꿀꺽', 조금씩 마시면 '홀짝홀짝'이라고 해요. 놀라거나 긴장했을 때 '침을 꿀꺽 삼키다'라고 하고, '남의 것을 말없이 가지다'는 뜻으로도 입말에서 써요.

phrases.en: The child gulped down the milk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 번 계속 삼키는 소리와 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the sound and look of swallowing many times in a row.

phrases.en: I was nervous, so I gulped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 긴장했을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for when you are surprised or tense.

phrases.en: I swallowed it in one gulp without chewing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씹지 않고 한 번에 넘기는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes swallowing something whole in one go.

explain_en: 꿀꺽 is the sound and look of swallowing food or water in one big gulp. Repeated gulps are '꿀꺽꿀꺽' and small sips are '홀짝홀짝'. When surprised or tense you '침을 꿀꺽 삼키다', and in casual speech it can also mean quietly taking something that is not yours.

examples.en: Adding mung bean sprouts to bibimbap makes it crunchy and tasty.
I lightly blanch mung bean sprouts and season them as a side dish.
I bought a bag of mung bean sprouts at the market.
I piled lots of bean sprouts on my rice noodles.

examples.ko: 숙주나물이 상하기 쉬워서 빨리 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Mung bean sprouts spoil easily, so you need to eat them quickly.

examples.ko: 어머니가 만든 숙주나물 무침이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The seasoned bean sprouts my mother makes are the tastiest.

explain: 콩나물과 비슷하게 생겼지만 콩나물은 콩으로, 숙주나물은 녹두로 키워요. 줄여서 '숙주'라고도 하고, 쌀국수에 넣는 숙주도 같은 재료예요.

phrases.en: Please put a lot of bean sprouts in the rice noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙주나물'을 줄인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 숙주나물.

phrases.en: I made seasoned mung bean sprouts as a side dish for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반찬 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used as the name of a side dish.

phrases.en: I blanched the mung bean sprouts quickly in boiling water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common action when cooking them.

explain_en: It looks like '콩나물' (soybean sprouts), but '콩나물' is grown from soybeans and '숙주나물' from mung beans. It is often shortened to '숙주', and the sprouts put in rice noodle soup are the same ingredient.
